entries.title: CFTC files interim final rule excluding casino-style gambling products from the "swap" definition
entries.facts: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed an interim final rule, "Further Definition of 'Swap' to Exclude Casino-Style Gambling Products" (RIN 3038-AF81, 17 CFR part 1), for public inspection with the Federal Register on October 16, 2026 at 8:45 a.m. ET as document 2026-21376, a 37-page document scheduled for publication on October 19, 2026. The SUMMARY states that the Commission "is adopting an interim final rule to codify its longstanding position that casino-style gambling products, including wagers placed on sportsbooks and casino games, are excluded from the 'swap' definition." The DATES section states that the interim final rule is effective on the date of publication in the Federal Register and that comments must be received 30 days after the date of publication. The public inspection text carries unfilled date brackets, so no calendar effective date or comment deadline appears on the face of the document. Comments reference RIN 3038-AF81 and are submitted through Regulations.gov or to the Secretary of the Commission. A companion notice of proposed rulemaking, RIN 3038-AF82, was filed in the same minute.
entries.relevant_to: sportsbooks and casino operators, prediction-market platforms, event-contract exchanges, derivatives intermediaries

entries.title: CFTC files proposed rule to define event contracts, including sports and politics contracts, as swaps
entries.facts: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed a notice of proposed rulemaking, "Further Definition of 'Swap' - Inclusions" (RIN 3038-AF82, 17 CFR part 1), for public inspection with the Federal Register on October 16, 2026 at 8:45 a.m. ET as document 2026-21377, a 36-page document scheduled for publication on October 19, 2026. The SUMMARY states that, "[c]onsistent with its jurisdiction over swaps," the Commission "is proposing to further define the term 'swap' to explicitly include event contracts, including those based on sports-, politics-, cultural-, and weather-related events." The DATES section states that comments must be received 30 days after the date of publication in the Federal Register; the public inspection text carries an unfilled date bracket, so no calendar comment deadline appears on the face of the document. Comments reference RIN 3038-AF82. A companion interim final rule, RIN 3038-AF81, excluding casino-style gambling products from the swap definition, was filed in the same minute.
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract exchanges, designated contract markets, sportsbooks, derivatives intermediaries
